title: Properties & Classification of Materials Practice Exam
description: Practice observing, comparing, and classifying materials using evidence.

questions.question: Which property tells how a material feels when you touch it?
questions.explanation: Texture describes how a material feels, such as smooth, rough, soft, or bumpy.

questions.question: A material should be classified by evidence, not by guessing.
questions.explanation: Scientific classification uses observations and test results as evidence.

questions.question: A material that can bend easily is called ________.
questions.explanation: Flexibility means a material can bend without breaking easily.

questions.question: Which material is most likely absorbent?
questions.explanation: A towel soaks up water, so it is absorbent.

questions.question: Why is a property table useful when studying materials?
questions.correctAnswer: It helps organize observations so materials can be compared and classified using evidence.
questions.explanation: A strong answer mentions organizing observations, comparing materials, and using evidence.

questions.question: Which pair belongs in the magnetic group?
questions.explanation: Iron and many steel objects are attracted to magnets.

questions.question: All metals are magnetic.
questions.explanation: Some metals are magnetic, but not all metals are attracted to magnets.

questions.question: Give one example of a material that is helpful in one setting but harmful in another.
questions.correctAnswer: Glass is useful as a window, but broken glass is harmful because it can cut people.
questions.explanation: A strong answer names a material, a useful setting, and a harmful setting.

questions.question: Which property tells whether a material is attracted to a magnet?
questions.explanation: Magnetism tells whether a material is attracted to a magnet.

questions.question: Salt can dissolve in water, so salt is ________ in water.
questions.explanation: A material that dissolves in water is called soluble.

questions.question: Plastic usually does not absorb water.
questions.explanation: Plastic is usually non-absorbent, which is why it is often used to keep things dry.

questions.question: Which material is best for drying wet hands?
questions.explanation: A towel is absorbent, so it is best for drying wet hands.

questions.question: A student grouped sponge and cloth together. What property could the student have used? Give one reason.
questions.correctAnswer: The student could have used absorbency because both sponge and cloth soak up water.
questions.explanation: A strong answer names a property and gives evidence from an observation or test.

questions.question: Which material is most suitable for the metal part inside an electric wire?
questions.explanation: Metal is used inside wires because it conducts electricity.

questions.question: Why is it important to use the same criteria when classifying materials?
questions.correctAnswer: It keeps the groups fair, clear, and based on one rule.
questions.explanation: A strong answer mentions fairness, clarity, and using one rule for all materials.
